title_zh: 帕瓦罗蒂你真吵-德国绘本大奖
source_file: 帕瓦罗蒂你真吵-德国绘本大奖（3-6岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 帕瓦罗蒂，
你真吵
[德]索菲·施密德 著 任庆莉 译
河北出版传媒集团 河北少年儿童出版社

[P2] 帕瓦罗蒂是一只小刺猬，他是夜行性动物。这天，他像往常一样坐在自己最喜欢的那棵大树的树杈上，等着月亮升起来。

他开始唱歌了。通常他会唱到深夜，有时甚至会唱到第二天早晨。

他唱得还不错，歌声高亢，持久回荡。

帕瓦罗蒂坚信自己是一只夜莺。身为一只会唱歌的夜莺，是多么幸运哪！

[P3] 可是住在他周围的邻居们就不那么幸运了，帕瓦罗蒂唱歌的声音太大了，吵得他们都睡不好。

兔子把青草塞到耳朵眼儿里，老鼠把树根里的洞打得再深一些。但是这一切都不管用！

小刺猬的歌声破坏了夜晚的宁静，松鼠和獾忍受不了了。狐狸甚至在想是不是该把这只刺猬吃掉，不过他很快就为自己有这个想法而感到羞愧。

[P4] 在一场漫长的“演唱会”之后，狐狸召集大家开会，当然
没有叫上帕瓦罗蒂，反正他白天总是在呼呼大睡。
大家一致同意，必须阻止帕瓦罗蒂继续唱歌。
“怎么才能阻止他呢？”
“只要我们能够说服他，让他知道自己不是一只夜莺，而是一只刺猬，他就不会再唱歌了。”松鼠说。
大家都表示赞成。为了说服帕瓦罗蒂，他们制订了周密的计划。

[P5] “计划一，我们先找帕瓦罗蒂谈一谈，”狐狸说，“告诉他刺猬是不会在夜晚唱歌的。问他能否在白天唱歌，因为晚上我们要睡觉。”
“没错。”帕瓦罗蒂回答道，“可我不是刺猬呀，我是一只夜莺，夜莺就是要在夜里唱歌。”
“怎么能怪夜莺在夜里唱歌呢？”

[P6] “第二个计划是找一个
参照物。我们去找一只真正的
夜莺，让他和帕瓦罗蒂对
比一下。”狐狸说。

“你也一定注意到了，从长相看，你完全没有鸟的样子。”老鼠接着说。

“你自己看看，你们俩长得完全
不一样。”兔子说。

但帕瓦罗蒂不以为然，他说：“我就是一只与
众不同的夜莺啊！”说完他就走开了。第二个计划
也失败了。

[P7] “真荒唐！

獾闷闷不乐地说：‘你说你是一只鸟，
那你怎么不住在鸟巢里呢？’

‘是呀！’老鼠喊道，‘你根本不会筑
巢，因为你就不是鸟！’
‘更不是会唱歌的鸟！’狐狸粗声粗气
地说。

帕瓦罗蒂没有争辩，而是很镇定地把周围一
些能用的东西搬过来，筑了一个巢。虽然这个巢
看上去有点儿奇怪，但它确实是一个巢，大家只
能接受。第三个计划也失败了。

[P8] ……上他每天坐的那个树杈，然后一边
大声唱着歌一边
掉落下来！

大家紧张地屏住呼吸。帕瓦罗蒂当然不会飞，他重重地摔在了地上。“看见了吗？”他在地上打了个滚儿，然后站起身来说，“这简直是小菜一碟。”

“我当然会飞。”

“如果你是一只夜莺，那你应该会飞。”狡猾的狐狸说出了第四个计划。
“对呀，快飞给我们看一看！”大家喊道。
帕瓦罗蒂听后不动声色地爬……

[P9] 现在只剩下第五个计划了，是
最后而且是最重要的一个计划。
“如果你坚持说自己是一只夜莺，那你一定会下蛋。”松鼠对帕瓦罗蒂说道。
“帕瓦罗蒂应该会下蛋！”，
“完全同意！”，
于是接连几个白天，帕瓦罗蒂都
坐在巢里，聚精会神地“下蛋”，晚上，他还在唱歌。
他必须下一个蛋！
时不时有动物经过他的巢，看看他是否已经下了蛋。
但不管帕瓦罗蒂怎么努力，他就是下不了蛋。

[P10] 在下蛋问题被提出来之后的第四
天晚上，大家没有听到歌声，四周安
静得只听见风吹树叶的沙沙声。
大家好奇地聚集到帕瓦罗蒂坐着
的树下。
帕瓦罗蒂躺在树杈上，看上去很
伤心，很疲倦。“我可能真的不是一
只夜莺！”他抽泣着说。
大家都很高兴他们的计划终于成功了。太棒了，再也没
有歌声打扰他们了！太令人兴奋了，从今以后每天都可以美
美地睡个通宵了！
只有帕瓦罗蒂失魂落魄地坐在
自己喜爱的树杈上。

[P11] 可是没过几天，先是狐狸告诉松鼠，他觉得夜里没了歌声，心里总是空落落的。然后是兔子，他们觉得好奇怪，没有了帕瓦罗蒂的歌声，他们好像都不能入睡了。
老鼠甚至尝试在睡觉前自己先唱歌，因为没有帕瓦罗蒂的歌声，他们睡不好觉。但这个方法并没有起作用。

[P12] “必须改变现状！”
“不能再这样下去了。”獾说，“帕瓦罗蒂不再唱歌以后，情况越来越糟糕了，我们应该想想办法。”可大家坐在地上一筹莫展，不知道现在该怎么办。
“我们在帕瓦罗蒂睡觉时把一个蛋放在他的身下，”松鼠提议道，“等他醒来后，就会以为是自己下了个蛋。”
“好主意！”
“就这么干！”
“完全同意！”
大家都很兴奋。于是等帕瓦罗蒂睡着后，松鼠悄悄地把一个蛋放在了他的身下。

[P13] “又回到了从前，真好！”
大家如释重负地说。现在他们可以在帕瓦罗蒂歌声的陪伴下安心地入睡了。

“我就知道我能行！”

第二天早晨，大家被一阵愉快的歌声唤醒了。
帕瓦罗蒂激动地喊道：“我下蛋啦！我是一只夜莺，一只可以尽情歌唱的夜莺！”他兴奋得唱了整整一天。

从此以后，每天晚上大家又能听到帕瓦罗蒂的歌声了。不过，令人欣喜的是，他再也不会唱到深夜，也不会唱到第二天天亮了，而是每晚用一首轻柔的催眠曲结束自己的“演唱会”。
full_text_en:
[P1] Pavarotti,
You're so noisy
[Germany] Sophie Schmid, author; Ren Qingli, translator
Hebei Publishing and Media Group, Hebei Children's Publishing House

[P2] Pavarotti is a little hedgehog, a nocturnal animal. This day, he sat as usual on his favorite tree branch, waiting for the moon to rise.

He began to sing. Usually, he would sing until late at night, sometimes even until the next morning.

He sang quite well, his voice high and resonant, echoing for a long time.

Pavarotti firmly believed he was a nightingale. How lucky to be a singing nightingale!

[P3] But the neighbors living around him weren't so lucky. Pavarotti's singing was too loud, and it kept them all from sleeping well.

Rabbits stuffed grass into their ears, and mice dug their holes deeper in the tree roots. But none of it worked!

The little hedgehog's singing ruined the peace of the night. The squirrel and badger couldn't stand it anymore. The fox even thought about eating the hedgehog, but he quickly felt ashamed of having such an idea.

[P4] After a long 'concert', the fox called everyone to a meeting, of course
without inviting Pavarotti, since he was always sleeping soundly during the day.
Everyone agreed that they must stop Pavarotti from singing anymore.
"How can we stop him?"
"As long as we can convince him that he is not a nightingale, but a hedgehog, he won't sing anymore," said the squirrel.
Everyone agreed. To convince Pavarotti, they made a careful plan.

[P5] "Plan one, let's talk to Pavarotti first," said the fox, "tell him hedgehogs don't sing at night. Ask if he can sing during the day, because we need to sleep at night."
"Correct," Pavarotti replied, "but I'm not a hedgehog. I'm a nightingale, and nightingales sing at night."
"How can we blame a nightingale for singing at night?"

[P6] "The second plan is to find a reference. Let's find a real nightingale and have him compare with Pavarotti," said the fox.

"You must have noticed, from appearance, you don't look like a bird at all," the mouse continued.

"Look for yourself, you two look completely different," said the rabbit.

But Pavarotti didn't think so. He said, "I am a unique nightingale!" Then he walked away. The second plan also failed.

[P7] "Nonsense!"

The badger said grumpily, "You say you're a bird,
then why don't you live in a bird's nest?"

"That's right!" the mouse shouted, "You can't even build
a nest, because you're not a bird!"
"And certainly not a singing bird!" the fox said gruffly.

Pavarotti didn't argue, but calmly gathered some usable things from around and built a nest. Although the nest looked a bit strange, it was indeed a nest, and everyone had to accept it. The third plan also failed.

[P8] ……onto the branch he sits on every day, then, while
singing loudly, he
falls down!

Everyone held their breath nervously. Of course, Pavarotti couldn't fly; he landed heavily on the ground. "See?" he rolled on the ground, then stood up and said, "This is a piece of cake."

"I can fly, of course."

"If you're a nightingale, then you should be able to fly." The sly fox announced the fourth plan.
"Right, fly for us to see!" everyone shouted.
Pavarotti, after hearing this, calmly began to climb...

[P9] Now there was only the fifth plan left, the last and most important one.
"If you insist you are a nightingale, then you must lay an egg," said the squirrel to Pavarotti.
"Pavarotti should lay an egg!"
"Completely agree!"
So for several days in a row, Pavarotti sat in his nest, concentrating hard on 'laying an egg'; at night, he was still singing.
He must lay an egg!
Animals would occasionally pass by his nest, checking to see if he had laid an egg yet.
But no matter how hard Pavarotti tried, he just couldn't lay an egg.

[P10] On the fourth night after the egg-laying issue was raised, no one heard the singing. The surroundings were quiet, with only the rustling of leaves in the wind.
Curious, everyone gathered under the tree where Pavarotti was sitting.
Pavarotti lay on a tree branch, looking very sad and tired. "I might really not be a nightingale!" he sobbed.
Everyone was delighted that their plan had finally succeeded. Wonderful! No more singing to disturb them! So exciting! From now on, they could sleep soundly through the night!
Only Pavarotti sat listlessly on his beloved tree branch.

[P11] But after a few days, first the fox told the squirrel that he felt the night was empty without the singing, and his heart felt hollow. Then the rabbits, they felt strange—without Pavarotti's singing, they seemed unable to fall asleep.
The mice even tried singing themselves before bed, because without Pavarotti's song, they couldn't sleep well. But this method didn't work.

[P12] "We must change the situation!"
"We can't go on like this," said the badger. "Since Pavarotti stopped singing, things have gotten worse and worse. We should think of a solution." But everyone sat on the ground, at a loss, not knowing what to do next.
"When Pavarotti is asleep, we'll put an egg under him," suggested the squirrel. "When he wakes up, he'll think he laid it himself."
"Good idea!"
"Let's do it!"
"Completely agree!"
Everyone was excited. So, after Pavarotti fell asleep, the squirrel quietly placed an egg under him.

[P13] "Back to the way it was, how wonderful!"
Everyone said with relief. Now they could fall asleep peacefully accompanied by Pavarotti's singing.

"I knew I could do it!"

The next morning, everyone was awakened by a cheerful song.
Pavarotti excitedly shouted, "I laid an egg! I'm a nightingale, a nightingale who can sing to my heart's content!" He sang joyfully all day.

From then on, everyone could hear Pavarotti's singing every evening again. However, happily, he no longer sang until late at night or until the next day dawned, but instead ended his "concert" each evening with a gentle lullaby.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，展示了一只戴着羽毛头饰、张开嘴巴的刺猬形象，标题为《帕瓦罗蒂，你真吵》，并标注了作者、译者和出版社信息。
[P2] 本页介绍了小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂在夜晚坐在树上等待月亮升起，随后开始唱歌，并坚信自己是一只会唱歌的夜莺。
[P3] 小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂的歌声太大，吵得周围的动物邻居们无法入睡，兔子、老鼠、松鼠、獾和狐狸都深受其扰，狐狸甚至一度想吃掉他，但很快感到羞愧。
[P4] 在小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂的歌声扰民后，狐狸召集兔子、老鼠、獾、松鼠等动物开会，大家一致决定阻止他继续唱歌，并商讨对策，最终决定通过说服他认清自己是刺猬而非夜莺来解决问题，为此制定了周密的计划。
[P5] 动物们试图说服小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂在白天唱歌，但他坚持自己是夜莺，必须在夜里歌唱，动物们对此感到无奈。
[P6] 动物们试图通过找一只真正的夜莺与帕瓦罗蒂对比，来证明他不是夜莺，但帕瓦罗蒂不以为然，坚持自己是与众不同的夜莺，导致第二个计划失败。
[P7] 动物们试图通过让小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂筑巢来证明他不是鸟，但他用各种杂物筑了一个巢，动物们无奈接受，第三个计划失败。
[P8] 动物们实施第四个计划，要求小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂证明自己会飞，但他从树上跳下后重重摔在地上，却仍坚持说自己会飞，动物们对此感到无奈。
[P9] 动物们实施第五个计划，要求小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂证明自己是夜莺就必须下蛋，他连续几天在巢里努力尝试，但始终无法下蛋，计划再次失败。
[P10] 在动物们要求小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂下蛋的计划失败后，第四天晚上他不再唱歌，动物们以为计划成功而欢呼庆祝，但帕瓦罗蒂却伤心地意识到自己可能不是夜莺，独自失魂落魄地坐在树杈上。
[P11] 动物们在没有帕瓦罗蒂歌声的夜晚感到空落落的，无法入睡，连老鼠尝试自己唱歌也无济于事。
[P12] 动物们因帕瓦罗蒂不再唱歌而感到困扰，决定实施新计划：在帕瓦罗蒂睡觉时悄悄在他身下放一个蛋，希望他醒来后会以为自己下蛋，从而证明他是夜莺。
[P13] 小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂在动物们悄悄为他准备的蛋旁醒来，误以为自己下蛋成功，激动地宣称自己是夜莺并重新开始歌唱。动物们因此重获安宁，帕瓦罗蒂也调整了歌唱时间，每晚以催眠曲结束。
[P14] 画面中，小刺猬帕瓦罗蒂站在树枝上，张大嘴巴兴奋地歌唱，身旁的鸟巢里有一只小鸟，背景是明亮的黄色圆月，整体氛围欢快而宁静。
